newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU releases aid to former Vulkan east German yards.
newsitem.headline: EU releases aid to former Vulkan east German yards.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had approved the payment of most of the one billion marks in subsidies by the German authorities to rescue the former subsidiaries of bankrupt shipyard Bremer Vulkan.

EU industry ministers agreed in April to a new aid programme for MTW Schiffswerft in Wismar and Volkswerft in Stralsund, both in the state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, but the Commission had still to unblock the money.

The amount consists of 180.5 million marks for MTW and 210.8 million marks for Volkswerft in operating aid, mainly to cushion massive redundancies at the yards, and investment aid of 195.3 million marks for MTW and 283 million marks for Volkswerft, the Commission said.
The Commission last year criticised Bremer Vulkan, accusing it of misusing large amounts of aid intended for its east German subsidiaries.
But it pledged to take an understanding attitude to the two yards, which were taken over by the regional state after Vulkan collapsed.
